subject: skill/stack/systemd
claim: Author service units with a [Service] section and choose Type= deliberately: exec (or simple) for long-running daemons and oneshot for run-to-completion jobs (add RemainAfterExit= if the unit should remain 'active'). For long-running services set Restart=on-failure — the manual's recommended choice for reliability — or always; ExecStop= plus TimeoutStopSec= govern graceful shutdown before SIGKILL. Auto-restart is rate-limited by StartLimitIntervalSec=/StartLimitBurst=, so a crash-looping unit eventually stops and stays failed rather than restarting forever.
notes: Single-source: only the systemd.service man page has fetched text, and it backs Type= semantics (simple/exec/forking/oneshot), the Restart= cause/effect matrix and the on-failure recommendation, ExecStop=/TimeoutStopSec= shutdown behavior, and start rate limiting. No companion source (e.g. systemd.unit/systemd.kill) is in the corpus, so uncertainty is raised. The repo's host-side agentic-dynamics-launch-broker.service should follow the on-failure recommendation with a bounded start limit.
